name: United Nations (UN)
principal_organs: UN Security Council (5 Permanent members: US, UK, France, Russia, China with veto power)
mission: Maintaining international peace and security, developing friendly relations among nations, achieving international cooperation, and harmonizing actions of nations.
description: The world's largest, most familiar, and most internationally represented intergovernmental organization, established following World War II to prevent future global conflict.

name: European Union (EU)
founded: 1 November 1993 (Maastricht Treaty; roots in 1957 Treaty of Rome)
core_pillars: Single internal market with four freedoms: free movement of goods, capital, services, and people
Common currency (Euro €) administered by the European Central Bank across 20 Eurozone countries
Common foreign, security, and environmental policies
description: A unique political and economic union of 27 European member states that operate an internal single market through a standardized system of laws applied in all member states.

name: North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)
core_principle: Collective Defense under Article 5: An attack against one member ally is considered an attack against all member allies.
mission: Guaranteeing the freedom and security of its members through political and military means, initially formed as a deterrent against Soviet expansion in post-war Europe.
description: An intergovernmental military alliance between 30 European and 2 North American countries committed to collective defense and transatlantic security cooperation.

name: Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)
mission: Accelerating economic growth, social progress, and cultural development in the region, promoting regional peace and stability through respect for justice and the rule of law.
description: A prominent regional grouping in Southeast Asia that promotes economic, political, and security cooperation among its ten member countries.
